name: Michael Quirk
current_role: Founder of Securipolis, a Sarasota cybersecurity firm
bio: Michael J. Quirk is a no-party-affiliation candidate for Florida's 17th Congressional District who reports a thirty-year career in data center, network and cybersecurity work for banks, airlines and tech firms. He moved to Sarasota in 2024, founded the cybersecurity firm Securipolis, and chairs a regional chapter of the International Association of Privacy Professionals. He says he mostly voted Republican before running as an independent.

platform.point: No Social Security or Medicare benefit cuts or retirement-age increases; top earners would pay payroll tax on all income.
Keep Medicare drug price negotiation and insulin caps, and extend ACA premium tax credits.
End blanket tariffs, restore open trade with Canada and Mexico, and require congressional votes on major tariffs.
Create a federal catastrophic reinsurance backstop, reauthorize flood insurance long term, and speed FEMA claims.
Require warrants for government surveillance, close the data-broker loophole, and pass a federal privacy law.
Require consent and payment for AI training data and disclosure when political ads use AI-generated content.
No sustained conflict without congressional authorization; repeal old war authorizations and attach conditions to military aid.
Supports open primaries, ranked choice voting, term limits, a congressional stock trading ban and no budget, no pay.

economy.evidence: Proposes applying payroll tax to all earnings of top earners and defends Medicare drug price negotiation, while opposing blanket tariffs.

welfare.evidence: Opposes Social Security and Medicare cuts, backs extending ACA premium tax credits and mental health coverage parity.

liberty.evidence: Supports the Second Amendment and opposes gun bans, would vote against a national abortion ban, and backs equal LGBTQ rights while keeping women's sports for biological women.

security.evidence: Opposes renewing warrantless surveillance authority without a warrant requirement and wants to bar government purchase of data it cannot seize without a warrant.

immigration.evidence: General statement: calls for a secure border alongside fixing legal immigration so it runs on predictable timelines.

foreign.evidence: Opposes wars without congressional authorization and 'blank checks' for any country, calling for conditions and separate votes on military aid.

energy.evidence: Proposes nuclear power first, rooftop solar before farmland, and full Everglades restoration funding; general on climate policy.

tech.evidence: Backs a federal privacy law, AI rules including chatbot privacy, consent and payment for AI training data, and cybersecurity standards for infrastructure.

notes: Positions come from the campaign issues and about pages (michaelquirkforcongress.com); search engines were unavailable, so no news coverage or questionnaires were reviewed. No stated position was found on education or religion in public life.

name: Deva Simmons
bio: Deva Simmons is a No Party Affiliation candidate for Florida's 18th Congressional District. A Brooklyn native who moved to Florida in 1995 and has lived in Polk County since 2002, she reports more than 20 years working in education. She has served on the board of the Boys & Girls Club of Lakeland and volunteers with kidsPACK and Polk County Schools.

platform.point: Calls health care a right; wants to protect and expand the Affordable Care Act and lower drug costs for seniors.
Raise teacher pay, expand early childhood education, make college more affordable, and protect public schools from defunding.
Raise the minimum wage to a living wage and protect workers' right to organize.
Support small businesses and create well-paying jobs in clean energy.
Protect voting rights, oppose gerrymandering, reform campaign finance laws, and increase government transparency.

economy.evidence: Campaign platform calls for raising the minimum wage to a living wage and protecting workers' right to organize.

welfare.evidence: Says health care is a right and pledges to protect and expand the Affordable Care Act and community health centers.

energy.evidence: General statement: lists creating good-paying jobs in clean energy among economic priorities.

education.evidence: Pledges to protect public schools from defunding and raise teacher pay.

notes: Positions come from the campaign home and issues pages (devasimmons.com); search engines were unavailable, and her interview videos were not reviewed. No stated position was found on social issues, policing, immigration, foreign policy, tech or religion.

name: Seth Haskin
bio: Seth Haskin is a 26-year-old No Party Affiliation candidate for Florida's 19th Congressional District who describes himself as a strict constitutionalist. He holds a bachelor's degree in neuroscience and says he grew up working in family small businesses. He says his Christian faith shapes his view that government should be limited.

platform.point: Repeal the 16th Amendment to end the federal income tax and restrain federal spending and borrowing.
Move toward a dollar backed by gold, silver, platinum and copper.
Repeal remaining Patriot Act surveillance authorities, strengthen warrant requirements, and end bulk collection of Americans' data.
Restore congressional war powers, reduce overseas military commitments, and oppose regime-change wars.
Repeal the 17th Amendment so state legislatures again choose U.S. senators.
Expand the House by 100 to 200 seats and require reapportionment review after every census.
Restore the nondelegation doctrine and return Congress to its enumerated powers.

economy.evidence: Supports repealing the 16th Amendment to end the federal income tax and moving toward a metal-backed dollar.

security.evidence: Pledges to repeal remaining Patriot Act surveillance authorities and opposes bulk collection of Americans' data.

foreign.evidence: Wants to reduce overseas military commitments and bases, oppose regime-change wars, and require congressional authorization for hostilities.

notes: Positions come from the campaign home, policy and about pages (sethhaskinforfl.com); some listings spell his name Haskins. Search engines were unavailable, and no stated positions were found on welfare, social issues, immigration, energy, tech, education or religion in public life.

name: Kedner Maxime
current_role: Pastor and founder of Advantage Tax Firm Consulting Services
bio: Kedner Maxime is the Independent Party of Florida candidate for Florida's 20th Congressional District. He came to the U.S. from Haiti in 1981 and founded Advantage Tax Firm Consulting Services in 1996. He has been a pastor at L'Eglise la Voix du Salut for 16 years and hosted a program on WLQY 1320AM.

platform.point: Secure borders, deport people who commit crimes, and create a pathway to citizenship and family reunification.
Lower drug costs, protect coverage for pre-existing conditions, and strengthen community health centers.
Raise public-school funding and teacher salaries and expand vocational training and apprenticeships.
Expand affordable housing and support first-time homebuyer assistance.
Support wages that match local living costs and protect the right to organize.
Cut federal red tape, simplify small-business tax filing, and expand SBA lending and micro-lending.
Protect Social Security and Medicare from cuts.
Publish every vote with plain-language reasoning and hold regular town halls in the district.

economy.evidence: Backs fair wages tied to living costs, the right to organize and action against price gouging, while also calling for cutting small-business red tape.

welfare.evidence: Calls health care a right and pledges to expand access to affordable care and defend Social Security and Medicare.

immigration.evidence: Supports a pathway to citizenship, family reunification and faster processing, with deportation focused on people who commit crimes.

education.evidence: Pledges to raise public-school funding and teacher salaries.

notes: Positions come from the campaign issue pages (maximeforcongress.com); search engines were unavailable, so no news coverage or questionnaires were reviewed. No stated positions were found on social issues, policing, foreign policy, energy, tech or religion in public life.

name: Alexander Cooke
current_role: Former mayor of Juno Beach; founder and CEO of Optimist Capital
bio: Alexander Cooke is a no-party candidate for Florida's 21st Congressional District. He was elected to the Juno Beach Town Council in 2022 and became mayor within a year. He founded Optimist Capital, a registered investment adviser, after a career in finance.

platform.point: Stop east-west discharges, send water south, and raise the federal cost share for the EAA Reservoir to 75 percent.
Tie federal funds to enforceable nutrient-load cuts in the Lake Okeechobee watershed with EPA backstop authority.
Make enhanced ACA subsidies permanent and extend the $2,000 drug out-of-pocket cap to marketplace plans.
Reform flood insurance and create a federally backstopped storm reinsurance pool plus home-hardening tax credits.
No Social Security cuts, retirement-age increases or privatization; let Medicare negotiate drug prices.
Require every foreign-aid supplemental to sunset and face a new vote; supports the next infrastructure bill.
Cut federal red tape, expand SBA-backed capital, and defend independent contractors.
Opposes the state Live Local Act's override of local zoning and institutional purchases of starter homes.

economy.evidence: Mixed: backs cutting small-business red tape and taxes on essentials, but also Medicare drug negotiation and a federally backstopped reinsurance pool.

welfare.evidence: Would cosponsor permanent enhanced ACA subsidies, extend the $2,000 drug cap to marketplace plans, and opposes Social Security cuts.

foreign.evidence: Wants every foreign-aid supplemental to sunset and require a new vote, and argues domestic spending should come ahead of foreign supplementals.

notes: Positions come from the campaign home, issues and meet-alex pages (alexcookeforcongress.com); search engines were unavailable, so Juno Beach council records and news coverage were not reviewed. No stated positions were found on social issues, policing, immigration, education or religion; his water-quality stance does not map clearly onto the energy scale.

name: Peter Jassenoff
bio: Peter Jassenoff is the Libertarian Party nominee for Florida's 25th Congressional District. No further public biographical information was found.
notes: Checked the Libertarian Party of Florida and national LP candidate pages, Wikipedia's race page and about a dozen likely campaign domains, but found no campaign site or statements. Search engines were unavailable in this pass, and all 10 topics remain unknown.

name: Deborah Ann Meidinger Hosey
current_role: Assistant director for elderly and veterans services (human services administrator)
bio: Deborah Ann Meidinger Hosey is an independent candidate for Florida's 26th Congressional District. She is a former teacher and Miami-Dade County Public Schools administrator who later worked as a Broward County human services administrator overseeing child care licensing and children's services. She also trained and worked as an EMT in New York.

platform.point: Create a merit-based legal pathway for undocumented people who self-report and pass screening, while maintaining a secure border.
Strengthen Social Security, Medicare and Medicaid and expand access to affordable, high-quality care.
Supports personal medical decisions with qualified professionals and financial help with adoption for women who choose it.
Fully fund IDEA and Section 504 for students with disabilities and expand career training and apprenticeships.
Lower rent, mortgage and insurance costs, increase housing supply, and expand homelessness prevention.
Tighten rules on stock trading and gifts, explore term limits, and revisit Citizens United.
Fully implement PACT Act protections and strengthen housing aid to reduce veteran homelessness.
Develop long-term deficit reduction strategies and strengthen fraud and waste prevention.

welfare.evidence: Pledges to strengthen Social Security, Medicare and Medicaid and says affordable health care for all ages is essential.

liberty.evidence: General statements: supports personal medical decision-making (abortion is not named), backs safety measures that respect responsible gun owners, and supports anti-discrimination protections.

security.evidence: General statement: supports strong law enforcement partnerships for safe schools and neighborhoods alongside mental health crisis programs.

immigration.evidence: Proposes a merit-based legal pathway for undocumented immigrants who self-report and pass screening, and expanded lawful pathways.

energy.evidence: General statement: lists sustainable energy, clean energy innovation and balanced climate solutions among research priorities.

education.evidence: Calls for fully funding IDEA and Section 504 and strengthening education from early childhood through college.

notes: Positions come from the campaign home, issues and about pages (deborahforcongress.com); search engines were unavailable, so no news coverage was reviewed. No stated positions were found on foreign policy or tech, and her faith statement stresses individual freedom without a clear policy direction.

name: Eddy Rojas
bio: Eddy Rojas is a Cuban-born businessman who immigrated to Miami and started out parking cars. He founded World Valet Parking, Flashwash Eco-Friendly Car Wash and ER Services Group. He is running as an independent in Florida's 28th district.

platform.point: Cut burdensome regulations and lower taxes on small businesses to bring jobs to Miami.
Supports school choice, vocational training and more affordable higher education.
Support law enforcement, secure the borders, and fund community crime-prevention programs for youth.
Lower prescription drug costs, expand telehealth, and protect Medicare for seniors.

economy.evidence: General statement: pledges to cut burdensome regulations and lower taxes on small businesses.

welfare.evidence: General statement: pledges to lower prescription drug costs, expand telehealth and protect Medicare.

security.evidence: General statement: pledges to support law enforcement, paired with community crime-prevention programs.

immigration.evidence: General statement: lists securing the borders under public safety.

education.evidence: General statement: lists school choice among his education priorities, alongside vocational training and affordable college.

notes: Positions come from the campaign priorities page (eddyrojas.com/events-1; the /issues link returns 404), and the bio comes from the first-round summaries plus his campaign about page. Search engines were unavailable, and no stated positions were found on social issues, foreign policy, energy, tech or religion in public life.
